title: Protect the starter
thesis: The slow invisible part of the work decides the result, long before anyone sees it.

nodes.text: Team leads reward the output they can see, so the slow groundwork goes unrewarded and unprotected.

evidence.filled_by: transcript line 11: "patience with the slow invisible part of the work"

nodes.text: By the time the output is visible, the result is already decided, and it can't be fixed at that stage.

evidence.filled_by: transcript line 5: "If the starter is weak, the loaves come out flat and sour and nobody can fix that at the oven."

nodes.text: Protect the unglamorous early work the way a baker protects the starter: the month of feeding it, the eleven years of notebooks.

evidence.filled_by: brief must_include.0: the month of feeding the starter
brief must_include.1: the eleven years of notebooks

nodes.text: What does protecting early work actually look like on a team? The brief has the bakery side of it but no team practice.
Which objection will a team lead raise first? The brief doesn't name one, so this part is held open.
First step: learn to see quality in the slow part, the way she knew he would be good before any loaf proved it.

evidence.filled_by: transcript line 9: "That was the moment she knew he would be good."
